name: Siemens S7-1500 / S7-1200 system and diagnostic messages
about: General Siemens knowledge for messages that do not come from the machine's own program: CPU diagnostic buffer events, error OBs, CPU LEDs, PROFINET faults, module and channel diagnostics, F-system (safety) messages, SINAMICS drive faults and communication errors. Each entry gives the meaning in plain English, likely causes, what to check and how to fix it. Wording of messages differs between firmware versions and languages, so entries are found by keywords, not exact text. Always confirm with the CPU diagnostic buffer or the device's own diagnostics (TIA Portal: Online & diagnostics, the CPU display, or the CPU web server).

entries.title: CPU is in STOP
entries.meaning: The PLC program is not running. Outputs go to their substitute values (usually off) and the machine stops. The CPU itself is still powered and reachable.
causes: Mode switch or display set to STOP, or someone stopped it from TIA Portal
A program error with no error handling (see the programming error and I/O access error entries)
Cycle time exceeded twice in one cycle
A STP instruction in the program
Startup failed: hardware differs from the configuration, missing or wrong memory card, or a download left the program inconsistent
F-CPU: the safety program found a fault and stopped
checks: Read the diagnostic buffer (TIA Portal: Online & diagnostics > Diagnostics > Diagnostic buffer, the CPU display, or the CPU web server). The newest entries before 'STOP' give the reason.
Look at the CPU LEDs: RUN/STOP yellow = STOP, ERROR red flashing = a fault is pending, MAINT yellow = maintenance needed.
Check the mode switch (S7-1500 has it behind the front flap, S7-1200 has no switch).
fixes: Fix the cause named in the diagnostic buffer first; otherwise the CPU will stop again.
Then switch to RUN with the mode switch, the display, or TIA Portal (Online tools > CPU operator panel > RUN).
If the program had to be changed, download it and check that online and offline match.
entries.cpuReaction: Program stops, outputs off (or substitute values), communication still works.

entries.title: Maximum cycle time exceeded (time error, OB80)
entries.meaning: One pass of the main program (OB1 and everything it calls, plus interrupts) took longer than the maximum cycle time set in the CPU properties (default 150 ms). The CPU calls the time error OB80. If the cycle runs past twice the maximum cycle time in the same cycle, the CPU goes to STOP whether or not OB80 exists.
causes: A loop in the program that runs too long or never ends (FOR/WHILE/REPEAT with a wrong end condition, waiting for an input inside a loop)
Large data copies or string handling every cycle
Too many or too slow cyclic interrupts (OB30-OB38) or hardware interrupts piling up
Heavy communication load (many HMI/OPC UA/web clients) on a small CPU
Maximum cycle time set too low for the program
checks: Diagnostic buffer: entry 'Cycle time exceeded' with the OB and the time.
TIA Portal: Online & diagnostics > Cycle time shows shortest, current and longest cycle.
Look for loops in the block that was running (the buffer entry often names it).
fixes: Fix the long-running code: limit loop counts, spread big jobs over several cycles, never wait inside a loop.
Only if the program really needs it: raise the maximum cycle time in CPU properties > Cycle (a program download).
Add OB80 to log the event if you want the CPU to keep running after a single overrun.
entries.cpuReaction: OB80 is called. Twice the maximum cycle time in one cycle: STOP.

entries.title: Programming error (OB121)
entries.meaning: An instruction could not be executed: for example an array index outside the array, a pointer or ANY to an address that does not exist, a call to a block or DB that is not in the CPU, or an access past the end of a DB. The diagnostic buffer names the block, the instruction (step address) and the kind of error.
causes: Array index computed from a value that went out of range (e.g. recipe number 0 or above the array size)
Indirect addressing (PEEK/POKE, ANY, VARIANT, DB_ANY) pointing to a missing or too short DB
A DB was deleted, renumbered or not downloaded
Partial download left blocks inconsistent
checks: Diagnostic buffer: 'Programming error' entry with block name, step address and error type. Double-click it in TIA Portal to jump to the code.
Check the index or pointer values in a watch table at the moment the error happens.
fixes: Check the index/pointer before using it (limit it to the array bounds), or handle errors locally with GET_ERR_ID / GET_ERROR in the block.
Download the full program so all blocks and DBs are consistent.
Add OB121 to log the error so the CPU does not stop, but still fix the cause.
entries.cpuReaction: S7-1500: STOP if OB121 is missing and the block does not handle the error itself. S7-1200: normally stays in RUN and only writes the buffer entry. Behaviour can depend on firmware, so read the buffer.

entries.title: I/O access error (OB122)
entries.meaning: The program tried to read or write an I/O address directly (with :P or a direct-access instruction) and the module did not answer: it is missing, failed, or the address is not configured.
causes: The module or PROFINET device at that address has failed or been pulled
Address used in the program does not exist in the hardware configuration
Device still starting up after power-on
checks: Diagnostic buffer: 'I/O access error' with the address and block.
Online & diagnostics: is the module at that address red?
fixes: Bring the module or device back (see module and PROFINET entries).
Correct the address in the program or the hardware configuration.
Add OB122 to log the error, and check the module's status before direct access.
entries.cpuReaction: Depends on CPU and firmware; usually stays in RUN with a buffer entry. Read the buffer.

entries.title: Diagnostic interrupt (OB82)
entries.meaning: A module or channel reported a fault (incoming) or that a fault has gone (outgoing). The real cause is in the module diagnostics: wire break, short circuit, missing supply, overflow and so on.
causes: A channel or module fault on a module with diagnostics enabled; see the channel entries for the specific fault
checks: Diagnostic buffer: the entry names the module (hardware identifier, slot) and the fault.
Online & diagnostics on that module: Diagnostic status and Channel diagnostics.
The module's red DIAG/channel LEDs.
fixes: Fix the named channel or module fault. The entry goes outgoing by itself once the cause is gone.
entries.cpuReaction: S7-1500/S7-1200 stay in RUN even without OB82.

entries.title: Module pulled or plugged (OB83)
entries.meaning: A configured module was removed (or reinserted) while the system was running, or stopped answering on the backplane.
causes: Module actually pulled or not fully engaged
Module failed
Backplane bus problem (bad U-connector on S7-1500, BaseUnit contact on ET 200SP)
Power to the module or station segment lost
checks: Diagnostic buffer and Online & diagnostics show which slot.
At the rack: is the module seated, are its LEDs on, is the front connector plugged?
fixes: Reseat or replace the module (same article number, or a compatible one).
Check the backplane connector and supply of that segment.
On S7-1500 central racks, power down before pulling modules unless the module allows hot swapping.
entries.cpuReaction: Stays in RUN; inputs of that module read as 0 or substitute value.
entries.safety: Switch off and lock out power before working in the cabinet unless you are authorised and the module is hot-swappable.

entries.title: Rack or station failure (OB86)
entries.meaning: A whole distributed I/O station (PROFINET IO device or PROFIBUS slave) stopped communicating. All its inputs read 0 or substitute values and its outputs go safe. When it comes back, a 'station return' entry follows.
causes: See 'PROFINET IO device failure'
checks: See 'PROFINET IO device failure'
fixes: See 'PROFINET IO device failure'
entries.cpuReaction: S7-1500 stays in RUN even without OB86.

entries.title: Startup blocked: configured and actual hardware differ
entries.meaning: At startup the CPU compares the hardware it finds with the downloaded configuration. Depending on the 'Comparison preset to actual module' setting, a wrong or missing module can stop the CPU from going to RUN.
causes: A module was replaced with a different article number or firmware
A module in the configuration is missing
Configuration downloaded for a different hardware build
checks: Diagnostic buffer: 'module type differs' / 'module missing' with the slot.
Compare the article numbers on the modules with the device configuration in TIA Portal.
fixes: Fit the configured module, or change the configuration to the module that is fitted and download it.
CPU properties > Startup > 'Comparison preset to actual configuration' decides whether a compatible module is accepted.
entries.cpuReaction: Stays in STOP until the configuration matches (when the CPU is set to require it).

entries.title: Memory card missing, wrong, full or write-protected
entries.meaning: S7-1500 always needs a SIMATIC Memory Card (it holds the program). S7-1200 can run from internal load memory, or use a card as program, transfer or firmware update card. A missing, faulty, full or wrongly prepared card stops the CPU or blocks downloads.
causes: Card pulled during operation (S7-1500 goes to STOP)
Card is not a Siemens SIMATIC Memory Card or is damaged
Load memory full (big project, too many saved trace/data logs/recipes)
S7-1200: card configured as transfer or firmware update card instead of program card
Card left write-protected after copying a project onto it
checks: Diagnostic buffer and CPU display: card status and memory usage.
TIA Portal: Online & diagnostics > Memory shows load memory used.
fixes: Insert the correct card, then power cycle or switch to RUN.
Free load memory (delete old data logs) or use a bigger card; download again.
Remove write protection or prepare the card again from TIA Portal (Card Reader/USB memory).
entries.cpuReaction: S7-1500 without a card: STOP, cannot start.

entries.title: Retentive data lost or reset (memory reset, reset to factory)
entries.meaning: Values kept through power-off (retentive DB data, counters, recipe data) were reset to their start values. This happens after a memory reset, a reset to factory settings, a download that reinitialises DBs, or a CPU or card change.
causes: Download of changed DB structure (TIA Portal reinitialises the DB)
Memory reset from the switch, display or TIA Portal
S7-1200: power loss without enough backup (retentive memory is limited)
checks: Diagnostic buffer: 'memory reset' or 'reinitialisation' entries.
Compare DB actual values with a snapshot or backup.
fixes: Restore values from a DB snapshot (TIA Portal: snapshot, then 'Copy snapshot to start values' / load) or re-enter recipes.
Use 'Download without reinitialization' with a memory reserve for future DB changes.

entries.title: CPU clock lost or not synchronised
entries.meaning: The CPU's real-time clock is wrong or was reset. Time stamps in alarms and the diagnostic buffer are then wrong, and time-of-day interrupts run at the wrong time.
causes: Long power-off: the clock is buffered only for a limited time (S7-1200 can use a battery board BB 1297)
NTP server not reachable or not configured
checks: Online & diagnostics > Set time; CPU properties > Time of day / NTP settings.
fixes: Set the time from TIA Portal or the display, or configure NTP to a reachable server.

entries.title: What the CPU LEDs mean (S7-1500 / S7-1200)
entries.meaning: RUN/STOP green = RUN; yellow = STOP; flashing yellow/green = starting up or a download. ERROR red flashing = a fault is pending (diagnostic, configuration or program error); ERROR red steady together with others = hardware fault. MAINT yellow = maintenance demanded or requested (for example a PROFINET device with a maintenance alarm), or forcing is active on some models. All LEDs flashing together = 'flash LED' test from TIA Portal to find the CPU. Port LEDs (LINK/RX/TX, green/yellow) show the Ethernet link per port.
checks: The diagnostic buffer explains every red or yellow LED; the S7-1500 display shows the same information under Diagnostics.
fixes: Find the entry in the diagnostic buffer and follow that entry's fix.

entries.title: Force job active
entries.meaning: Someone forced inputs or outputs from TIA Portal. Forced values stay in place even after the program or the operator wants something else, and they survive a power cycle. The MAINT (S7-1500) or MAINT/force LED (S7-1200) shows it.
causes: Commissioning or troubleshooting left forces active
checks: TIA Portal: Online, open the force table (Watch and force tables > Force table) to see what is forced.
fixes: Have a qualified person review the forced values and stop forcing (Stop forcing) once the reason is gone.
entries.safety: Forced outputs can move the machine regardless of program interlocks. Never force to bypass a safety function or interlock.

entries.title: Access protection / password / know-how protection
entries.meaning: The CPU's access level (full, read, HMI, no access) or a block's know-how or copy protection prevents an action such as going online with write rights, downloading, or opening a block.
causes: Protection level set in CPU properties > Protection & Security
Block protected by the OEM
Copy protection bound to another CPU serial number or card
checks: The message in TIA Portal names the protection; CPU properties show the access level.
fixes: Get the password from the owner of the project or the OEM. PLC-Ki only reads, so it needs read access at most.

entries.title: STOP caused by STP instruction
entries.meaning: The program itself put the CPU into STOP by calling the STP instruction, usually on purpose when it found a serious condition.
causes: The condition programmed in front of the STP call became true
checks: Diagnostic buffer names the block; search the program for STP to see the condition.
fixes: Find and fix the condition that triggers it, then switch to RUN.

entries.title: Online and offline program differ / inconsistent download
entries.meaning: The program in the CPU is not the same as the project open in TIA Portal (or the archive PLC-Ki was built from). Explanations based on the archive may then be wrong for the changed blocks.
causes: Changes downloaded from another PC
Download aborted
Archive is older than the running program
checks: TIA Portal: Go online, the compare icons show which blocks differ; Online > Compare offline/online.
fixes: Upload from the device into a new project to get the running version, or download the intended version. Then make a fresh archive for PLC-Ki.

entries.title: PROFINET IO device failure (station failure)
entries.meaning: The CPU (IO controller) lost cyclic communication with a PROFINET IO device: remote I/O, a drive, a valve terminal, a robot or another PLC. Its inputs read 0 or substitute values and the device puts its outputs in the safe state. The BF (bus fault) LED on the device and the ERROR LED on the CPU usually light up.
causes: Device has no power (check its 24 V supply, fuses, main switch of a drive)
Cable unplugged, damaged or a bad connector; a switch in between failed or is unpowered
Device name changed or lost (after replacing a device)
IP address conflict on the network
Device in the wrong network segment or blocked by a firewall/managed switch
Too much network load or a loop causing the watchdog (update time x accepted cycles) to run out
checks: Diagnostic buffer: 'IO device failure' with device name and time; repeated come/go means a loose contact or intermittent network.
Online & diagnostics > Topology view shows where the line breaks.
At the device: power LED, BF LED, port LINK LEDs on both ends of each cable.
TIA Portal: Accessible devices to see whether it answers and with which name/IP.
fixes: Restore power, cable or switch; replace a damaged cable or connector.
After a device swap, assign the PROFINET device name (Online > Assign device name) or use topology-based automatic commissioning ('device replacement without exchangeable medium').
Clear IP/name conflicts.
If it drops out intermittently, check cable routing near drives, shield grounding and the port statistics.
entries.cpuReaction: S7-1500/S7-1200 stay in RUN; OB86 is called if present.

entries.title: PROFINET device name missing or wrong
entries.meaning: The IO controller finds its devices by PROFINET device name. A new or reset device has no name (or the wrong one), so the controller cannot start communicating with it.
causes: Device replaced
Device reset to factory settings
Two devices with the same name
Name typed differently in the configuration
checks: TIA Portal: Online access > your adapter > Update accessible devices; compare names with the configuration.
Device BF LED flashing usually means 'no communication / name missing'.
fixes: Assign the name from the configuration (in the network view right-click the device > Assign device name).
Enable 'Support device replacement without exchangeable medium' with configured topology so replacements get their name automatically.

entries.title: IP address conflict / duplicate address
entries.meaning: Two devices on the same network use the same IP address. One or both stop communicating; on a CPU interface the port may be switched off for IP traffic.
causes: A laptop, HMI or replacement device set to an address already in use
Wrong address typed during commissioning
checks: Diagnostic buffer names the interface; 'Accessible devices' lists all devices and their addresses.
fixes: Give the newcomer a free address; keep an address list for the machine network.

entries.title: Topology error: wrong or missing port neighbour
entries.meaning: The configured topology says port X of one device connects to port Y of another, but the actual cabling is different or the link is down. Usually a maintenance message; it matters when automatic device replacement or IRT/MRP depends on the topology.
causes: Cable moved to another port
Cable missing or broken
Device added in the line
checks: Online & diagnostics > Topology view (offline/online comparison).
fixes: Plug cables as configured, or update the configured topology and download.

entries.title: Port link down / cable fault
entries.meaning: An Ethernet port lost its physical connection to the next device. Every device behind that point in a line topology is lost too.
causes: Cable unplugged or damaged
Connector badly crimped
Next device unpowered
Port disabled in configuration
checks: Port LINK LEDs at both ends.
Topology view shows the broken segment.
fixes: Replace or re-terminate the cable (industrial RJ45/M12), power the neighbour device.

entries.title: Media redundancy: ring open (MRP)
entries.meaning: The PROFINET ring has a break. The machine keeps running over the other direction, but redundancy is lost: one more break will cut devices off.
causes: A cable or port in the ring failed
A device in the ring was switched off
checks: Diagnostic buffer of the MRP manager; topology view; port LEDs along the ring.
fixes: Find and fix the broken segment soon, during the next stop.

entries.title: PROFINET watchdog / update time / communication overload
entries.meaning: Cyclic data did not arrive within the watchdog time (update time x number of accepted missing cycles), so the device or controller dropped the connection. Typically intermittent.
causes: Network overload or broadcast storm
A loop in unmanaged switches
EMC disturbances on cables near drives
Too short update time for the number of devices in a line
checks: Count how often the failure comes and goes in the diagnostic buffer.
Managed switch port statistics (errors, discards).
fixes: Separate office/IT traffic from the machine network, remove loops, improve shielding and routing.
Increase update time or accepted update cycles in the device's IO cycle settings if the process allows.

entries.title: Shared device / I-device not reachable
entries.meaning: A PLC that exchanges data with another PLC as an I-device (or a shared device used by two controllers) lost the connection to its partner. The transfer areas stop updating.
causes: Partner PLC in STOP or powered off
Configuration of the transfer areas changed on only one side
Network fault between them
checks: Diagnostic buffers of both PLCs; status of the partner PLC.
fixes: Bring the partner back to RUN; download matching configurations on both sides (the I-device GSD must be re-exported after changes).

entries.title: Maintenance required / maintenance demanded
entries.meaning: A device reports it still works but needs attention soon: for example a fibre-optic link losing power budget, MRP ring open, a fan, or a module with a long-term problem. The MAINT LED is yellow. The machine keeps running.
causes: Depends on the device; the diagnostic text names it
checks: Online & diagnostics on the device named in the buffer.
fixes: Plan the repair for the next stop.

entries.title: Device firmware or GSD does not match the configuration
entries.meaning: The device answers but rejects the configuration because its firmware or type does not match what the GSD/hardware catalog entry in the project expects.
causes: Replacement device with newer or older firmware
Wrong device variant ordered
checks: Diagnostic buffer and module information (Online & diagnostics > General) show actual firmware.
fixes: Update the device firmware, or change the configured version in TIA Portal and download.

entries.title: Wire break (channel diagnostics)
entries.meaning: The module detects that the circuit to a sensor or actuator is open. Analog inputs typically read 32767 (16#7FFF, 'overflow') when this happens, digital inputs with wire-break diagnostics need a sensor with a defined quiescent current or a resistor.
causes: Cable cut or pulled out of a terminal
Connector loose
Sensor/transmitter defective or unpowered (4-20 mA loop below about 1.2 mA)
Fuse in the loop blown
checks: Module DIAG and channel LEDs; Online & diagnostics > Channel diagnostics names the channel.
Measure at the terminal: voltage/current; for 4-20 mA check the loop current.
Check the front connector is fully screwed in.
fixes: Repair the wiring or replace the sensor; the diagnostic goes away once the channel reads a valid value.
entries.safety: Isolate the circuit before working on terminals; 4-20 mA loops may be powered from elsewhere.

entries.title: Short circuit to ground / to M
entries.meaning: A channel output, sensor supply or encoder supply is shorted to 0 V (M) or overloaded. The module switches that output off to protect itself.
causes: Damaged cable insulation
Defective solenoid coil or sensor
Wrong wiring after a change
Water in a junction box or connector
checks: Channel diagnostics names the channel.
Disconnect the field cable and measure insulation/resistance.
fixes: Repair the cable or replace the load; the output recovers once the short is gone (some modules need the channel switched off and on).
entries.safety: Isolate and lock out the circuit before measuring or repairing.

entries.title: Short circuit to L+ (supply)
entries.meaning: An output channel is connected to the 24 V supply in the field, so it cannot be switched off. The load may run even when the program switches the output off.
causes: Cable damage touching a 24 V conductor
Wiring error
checks: Channel diagnostics; measure the output with the channel off.
fixes: Find and repair the wiring fault.
entries.safety: The actuator may be energised regardless of the program; isolate it before working on the machine.

entries.title: Analog value overflow / underflow (measuring range exceeded)
entries.meaning: The analog signal is outside what the module can measure. Rated range is 0..27648 (or -27648..27648); 27649..32511 is overrange (still measured); 32767 means overflow, often a wire break or a short on 4-20 mA; -32768 means underflow (e.g. 4-20 mA below about 1.2 mA, or wire break on some modules).
causes: Sensor really out of range
Wire break or short circuit
Sensor type or range set wrong in the module parameters (e.g. 0-10 V configured, 4-20 mA wired)
Transmitter fault or saturating
checks: Raw value of the channel in a watch table.
Module parameters (measurement type and range) against the wiring.
Measure the signal at the terminal.
fixes: Repair wiring or sensor, or correct the module parameters and download.

entries.title: Supply voltage L+ / load voltage missing
entries.meaning: The 24 V that powers a module's outputs or sensors is missing. On ET 200SP this is the potential group fed by a light BaseUnit or power module. All outputs in that group stay off and sensor inputs read 0.
causes: Fuse or circuit breaker for the load supply tripped
Supply deliberately switched off by a safety relay or E-stop contactor (common: outputs are fed through the safety circuit)
Loose supply terminal or front connector bridge
checks: Module/power module diagnostic text and its PWR LED.
Measure 24 V at the supply terminals.
Is the E-stop or safety circuit open?
fixes: Reset or replace the fuse after finding why it tripped; restore the safety circuit through the normal reset.
entries.safety: If the supply comes through a safety circuit, never bridge it; reset the safety function properly.

entries.title: Module overtemperature
entries.meaning: The module's internal temperature is above its limit, often because outputs carry too much current or the cabinet is too hot.
causes: Cabinet cooling failed (fan, filter clogged, air conditioner)
Outputs loaded above rating or too many outputs on together
Module mounted outside its permitted orientation
checks: Cabinet temperature; output currents; filter mats.
fixes: Restore cooling; reduce load or spread it across modules.

entries.title: Parameter assignment error / module not parameterised
entries.meaning: The module rejected the parameters the CPU sent (for example a measuring range or mode it does not support), so the module or channel does not work.
causes: Module firmware older than the configured version
Parameters changed at runtime (WRREC) with invalid values
Wrong module variant
checks: Channel diagnostics; module firmware vs configured version.
fixes: Correct the parameters or module version in TIA Portal and download; update module firmware.

entries.title: Fuse blown / fuse missing
entries.meaning: A fuse in the module or front connector (some AC/relay modules) has blown; the channels behind it do not work.
causes: Short circuit or overload on the channels behind the fuse
checks: Module diagnostics; inspect the fuse.
fixes: Find and remove the short, then replace the fuse with the same rating.

entries.title: Reference junction / thermocouple compensation error
entries.meaning: A thermocouple input cannot compensate the cold junction temperature (the reference channel or internal sensor is faulty or misconfigured), so temperatures are wrong. Also covers RTD (Pt100) wiring faults on resistance inputs.
causes: Reference junction set to an external channel that is not wired
Wrong thermocouple type parameterised
RTD wire break or wrong 2/3/4-wire setting
checks: Channel parameters (type, reference junction) vs wiring.
fixes: Correct parameters or wiring.

entries.title: Channel or module temporarily not available / substitute value
entries.meaning: The channel cannot deliver a valid value right now (startup, firmware update, re-parameterisation, missing supply). With 'value status' enabled the module gives a status bit per channel (1 = valid).
causes: Module starting up or being updated
Supply missing
Channel switched off in parameters
checks: Value status bits; module diagnostics.
fixes: Wait for startup to finish or fix the named cause.

entries.title: ET 200SP: server module missing, wrong BaseUnit or empty slot
entries.meaning: An ET 200SP station needs a server module at the end and the BaseUnit types (light = opens a new potential group, dark = continues it) to match the configuration. A missing module, empty slot or wrong BaseUnit stops the station or the modules after it.
causes: Server module not fitted after changes
Module pulled leaving an empty BaseUnit
Light/dark BaseUnit swapped
checks: Interface module diagnostics; station LEDs; compare the station with the configuration slot by slot.
fixes: Fit the server module or the missing module (or a BU cover if configured as empty), use the configured BaseUnit types.

entries.title: F-I/O passivated (safety module or channel in safe state)
entries.meaning: A fail-safe module or channel detected a fault (discrepancy between two sensor channels, short circuit, wire break, PROFIsafe communication error) and switched to its safe state: fail-safe inputs read 0, outputs are off. After the fault is gone the module waits for a user acknowledgement (reintegration) before working again.
causes: Discrepancy: the two contacts of a 2-channel sensor (E-stop, door switch) did not switch together within the discrepancy time
Wire break or short on an F-channel; cross-circuit between channels
PROFIsafe communication timeout or CRC error (often a network problem)
F-module replaced or PROFIsafe address set wrongly
checks: F-I/O DB values: PASS_OUT, QBAD (or QBAD_I_xx/QBAD_O_xx), ACK_REQ = 1 means waiting for acknowledgement.
Diagnostic buffer and module channel diagnostics name the channel and fault.
Test the sensor: do both channels switch together?
fixes: Repair the sensor, wiring or network cause.
Then reintegrate with the machine's normal reset/acknowledge button (it drives ACK_REI or ACK_GL in the safety program).
Recurring discrepancy faults mean a worn or misaligned sensor: replace or adjust it.
entries.safety: Do not bridge or defeat safety sensors or circuits. Changes to the safety program or F-parameters need a qualified person and a safety acceptance test.

entries.title: PROFIsafe address (F-destination address) mismatch
entries.meaning: The F-module's PROFIsafe destination address (set by DIP switches or assigned electronically and stored in the coding element) does not match the configuration, so the module stays passivated.
causes: Replacement module without the address set
Coding element swapped or reset
checks: Module diagnostics: 'PROFIsafe address mismatch' / 'wrong F_Dest_Add'.
fixes: Assign the PROFIsafe address from TIA Portal (Assign PROFIsafe address, confirming the module by flashing LED) or set the DIP switches to the configured address, then reintegrate.
entries.safety: Only a qualified person may assign F-addresses; confirm you are addressing the right module.

entries.title: F-CPU: safety program stopped / safety mode error / signature mismatch
entries.meaning: The F-CPU found an internal or safety program error (for example corrupted data, an F-cycle time exceeded, or an inconsistent safety program after a partial download). It puts the safety program and usually the CPU into STOP. A deactivated safety mode or a changed collective signature means the running safety program is not the accepted one.
causes: F-runtime group cycle time exceeded
Safety program changed without a complete download
Hardware fault in the F-CPU
checks: Diagnostic buffer; Safety Administration editor in TIA Portal (collective signature, safety mode).
fixes: A qualified person compares the signature with the accepted one, downloads the accepted safety program completely and repeats the acceptance test if anything changed.
entries.safety: The machine must not run with a safety program that is not the accepted version.

entries.title: E-stop or guard door open (safety circuit not ready)
entries.meaning: A safety function is active: an emergency stop is pressed, a guard is open, or a light curtain is interrupted. The safety program or relay removes energy (contactor off, drive STO) until the cause is cleared and the circuit is reset.
causes: Someone pressed an E-stop or opened a guard
A safety switch is misaligned or faulty
Discrepancy fault on a 2-channel device (see F-I/O passivated)
checks: Which E-stops and guards are open (machine HMI or the F-DB inputs).
Pull out and check every E-stop on the line, including remote ones.
fixes: Release the E-stop / close the guard, then press the safety reset and the machine reset.
entries.safety: Never bridge an E-stop, guard switch or safety relay. If a safety device is faulty, have it repaired by a qualified person.

entries.title: SINAMICS F07900: Motor blocked
entries.meaning: The drive ran at its current limit for longer than the blocking time while the speed stayed below the blocking threshold: the motor cannot turn.
causes: Mechanical blockage (jammed product, seized bearing or gearbox, brake not released)
Load too high for the motor/drive
Motor brake not opening (brake control or supply)
Wrong motor data or current limit too low
checks: Can the shaft turn by hand (with power isolated)?
Is the holding brake releasing?
Drive parameters r0068 (current) and r0063 (speed) at the moment of the fault, via Startdrive or the BOP/IOP.
fixes: Remove the blockage, repair the mechanics or brake, then acknowledge the fault on the drive (or via the PLC reset).
Only if the load is correct: check motor data and current limit (p0640) with a drive specialist.
entries.safety: Isolate and lock out the drive before touching the mechanics; a blocked load can move suddenly when freed.

entries.title: SINAMICS F07901: Motor overspeed
entries.meaning: The motor turned faster than the maximum speed limit allows.
causes: Load driving the motor (lowering, unwinding) without enough braking
Speed controller badly tuned
Encoder fault
checks: Process situation at the time; encoder signal; braking resistor.
fixes: Check braking (resistor, regenerative unit), controller settings and encoder; acknowledge.

entries.title: SINAMICS F07011 / A07910: Motor overtemperature
entries.meaning: The motor temperature (measured by a PTC/KTY/Pt1000 sensor, or calculated by the drive's thermal model) is above the limit. A07910 is the warning, F07011 the trip.
causes: Motor overloaded for too long
Motor fan blocked or cooling fins dirty
Running at low speed with a self-cooled motor
Temperature sensor wire break (can look like overtemperature)
checks: Motor temperature r0035; motor current; fan and fins; sensor wiring.
fixes: Let it cool, remove the overload, clean the cooling, repair the sensor wiring; acknowledge.

entries.title: SINAMICS F30001 / F07801: Overcurrent
entries.meaning: The current in the power unit or motor went above the permitted limit and the drive switched off immediately.
causes: Short circuit or earth fault in the motor or motor cable
Acceleration ramp too steep for the load
Mechanical shock load
Wrong motor data, or a contactor opening/closing between drive and motor while running
checks: Insulation test of motor and cable (disconnected from the drive)
Ramp-up time p1120 and load at the time of the trip
fixes: Repair motor/cable faults, lengthen the ramp, never switch the motor contactor while the drive is running; acknowledge.
entries.safety: Isolate the drive and wait for the DC link to discharge (see the warning label, typically 5 minutes) before working on motor cables.

entries.title: SINAMICS F30002: DC link overvoltage
entries.meaning: The drive's DC link voltage went too high, usually because the motor fed energy back while braking and the drive had nowhere to put it.
causes: Ramp-down time too short for the load inertia
Braking resistor missing, broken or not enabled
Line voltage too high
checks: Ramp-down time p1121; braking resistor and its parameters; line voltage.
fixes: Lengthen the ramp-down, fit or repair the braking resistor, or enable the Vdc_max controller; acknowledge.

entries.title: SINAMICS F30003: DC link undervoltage
entries.meaning: The DC link voltage dropped too low while running, usually because the mains supply dipped or a phase is missing.
causes: Mains dip or interruption
Line contactor or fuse opened
Phase missing
checks: Mains voltage and fuses; line contactor; other drives tripping at the same time.
fixes: Restore the supply; acknowledge. If dips are frequent, consider kinetic buffering or automatic restart (by a drive specialist).

entries.title: SINAMICS F30004: Heat sink overtemperature
entries.meaning: The power unit's heat sink is too hot.
causes: Drive fan failed
Cabinet too hot or air flow blocked
Load too high
Pulse frequency set too high
checks: Drive fan; cabinet temperature and filters; load current.
fixes: Replace the fan, restore cabinet cooling, reduce load; acknowledge after cooling.

entries.title: SINAMICS F30005: Power unit overload (I2t)
entries.meaning: The power unit carried more current than its rating for too long, according to its thermal model.
causes: Load too high (process, mechanics)
Duty cycle too heavy for the drive size
Motor data wrong
checks: Current over time (trace); mechanics; recent process changes.
fixes: Reduce the load or fix the mechanics; a permanent overload needs a bigger drive.

entries.title: SINAMICS F30011: Line phase failure
entries.meaning: One of the three mains phases to the drive is missing.
causes: Blown fuse in one phase
Loose terminal
Contactor contact worn
checks: Measure all three phase voltages at the drive input; fuses; contactor.
fixes: Replace the fuse or repair the connection; acknowledge.
entries.safety: Measuring mains voltage is work for an electrically qualified person.

entries.title: SINAMICS F30021: Ground fault
entries.meaning: The drive detected current flowing to earth: the insulation of the motor or motor cable is damaged.
causes: Damaged motor cable
Wet or damaged motor winding
Moisture in a terminal box
checks: Insulation resistance test of cable and motor (disconnected from the drive).
fixes: Repair or replace the cable/motor; dry out terminal boxes; acknowledge.
entries.safety: Isolate and lock out; let the DC link discharge before disconnecting.

entries.title: SINAMICS F01910: Fieldbus setpoint timeout
entries.meaning: The drive stopped receiving its control word and setpoint from the PLC over PROFINET/PROFIBUS, so it stopped the motor.
causes: PLC in STOP
PROFINET cable or switch fault, device name lost
PLC program not writing the telegram (wrong address or DPWR_DAT not called)
checks: CPU in RUN? Is the drive shown failed in the PLC diagnostics (see IO device failure)?
Drive BF LED and network LEDs.
fixes: Restore the PLC or network; acknowledge the drive fault from the PLC (control word bit 7) or locally.

entries.title: SINAMICS F07860 / F07861 / F07862: External fault
entries.meaning: A signal wired into the drive (digital input or a bit from the PLC) that is configured as 'external fault' became active. The drive itself is fine; the real cause is the device that sets that signal.
causes: Motor thermal switch, pressure switch or other monitoring device opened
PLC set the external fault bit
checks: Which input is connected to p2106/p2107/p2108 (via Startdrive)
The wiring diagram for that input.
fixes: Clear the cause at the external device, then acknowledge.

entries.title: SINAMICS STO active (Safe Torque Off)
entries.meaning: The drive's safety function has removed torque from the motor (STO), usually because an E-stop or guard is open, or via PROFIsafe from the F-CPU. The drive shows 'switching on inhibited' until STO is deselected and the drive is switched on again (OFF1 then ON).
causes: E-stop, guard or safety relay open
PROFIsafe communication to the drive lost
Safety Integrated test stop due
checks: Safety circuit state; drive status word bit 'switching on inhibited'.
fixes: Clear the safety cause and reset it; the PLC must then send OFF1 followed by ON to the drive.
entries.safety: STO removes torque but does not isolate the drive from the mains; do not treat it as electrical isolation.

entries.title: PUT/GET access denied
entries.meaning: A partner (another PLC, SCADA, older HMI driver or third-party tool) tried to read or write the CPU with classic S7 PUT/GET communication, which S7-1500/S7-1200 block by default.
causes: 'Permit access with PUT/GET communication from remote partner' is not enabled
Access to optimised DBs (PUT/GET needs non-optimised DBs)
checks: CPU properties > Protection & Security > Connection mechanisms.
fixes: Enable PUT/GET only if the network is protected, and use non-optimised DBs for the exchanged data; download the hardware configuration.
entries.safety: PUT/GET allows writes without a password; enable it only on a protected machine network.

entries.title: Too many connections / connection resources exhausted
entries.meaning: The CPU has a fixed number of communication connections (HMI, PG, web, OPC UA, open user communication). When they are all in use, new clients cannot connect.
causes: Several HMIs, laptops, SCADA and web clients at once
Clients that do not close connections (open user communication with TCON without TDISCON)
checks: Online & diagnostics > Communication > Connection resources shows used and free connections.
fixes: Close unused clients, fix the program so it reuses connections, or reserve connections in CPU properties.

entries.title: HMI connection to the PLC lost
entries.meaning: The HMI panel or SCADA cannot reach the PLC: values show #### or the HMI shows a connection error. The PLC may still be running normally.
causes: Network cable or switch problem
PLC IP address changed or CPU in a different subnet
Connection resources exhausted
PLC powered off or memory card missing
checks: Ping the PLC from another device; check the CPU LEDs; diagnostic buffer for connection entries.
fixes: Restore the network or address; free connection resources; then restart the HMI runtime if it does not reconnect.

entries.title: Open user communication errors (TSEND_C / TRCV_C / TCON)
entries.meaning: A TCP/UDP/ISO-on-TCP link programmed in the PLC (for example to a scanner, robot, MES or another PLC) failed. The instruction's STATUS word gives the reason.
causes: Partner not reachable or not listening on that port
Connection closed by partner
Wrong connection parameters (IP, port, ID)
Temporary communication error
checks: The block's STATUS/ERROR outputs in a watch table, looked up in the TIA Portal help for that instruction.
Can the partner be pinged? Is it running?
fixes: Fix the partner or network; correct the parameters. The program should retry automatically after a temporary error.
